contributions.title: Relic's native server stalled whenever a handler waited
contributions.summary: On relic_native, any handler that waits on the database stalled: after each write the server held the event loop for 1 ms. The fix yields to the event loop first, so waiting handlers finish.

numbers.label: Serverpod on Relic native, read only

contributions.note: This benchmark, methodology v3, median of 3 rounds, before and with the fix.

contributions.title: Two flaky Serverpod database tests
contributions.summary: Found while testing the Serverpod speedups below: a serializable transaction test raced its own write, and a parallel-calls test left an unhandled error in setUpAll. Both reproduced with injected delays.

contributions.title: A faster Content-Type parser in Relic
contributions.summary: Every request parsed its Content-Type with a regular expression. The first fix, a cache, was turned down; the maintainer wrote a byte-level parser instead, which was merged.

contributions.title: Less work for every Serverpod request
contributions.summary: A CPU profile showed Serverpod capturing a stack trace for every database query, rebuilding the same SQL strings, and doing session work only logged sessions need. Three pull requests remove that work.
contributions.note: This benchmark, methodology v2.1, median of 3 rounds, with these and the postgresql-dart changes together.

contributions.title: Pooled Postgres connections reset too often
contributions.summary: The driver reset a pooled session after any UPDATE ... SET, and captured a stack trace on every pool checkout. Now it resets only when a query really changes session state, and records the trace only on failure. Each saves 3 to 5% of the CPU instructions of a Serverpod request that reads one row.

contributions.title: Dart's HTTP server and async stack traces
contributions.summary: Each small HTTP response sets up two stream controllers, about 11% of a Serverpod request's CPU. Separately, StackTrace.current looked up the same dart:async members on every call; the change caches them.
